We're preparing for an internal team meeting (organized by someone named "Tash") about Sprint 3 priorities for "all things components" on the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project — specifically a proposed NEW approach to writing UI User Stories: moving from broad UI User Stories that encompass a whole group of components toward smaller, isolated, individually-specified component stories.

Context we already have from prior sessions: the team already has a semi-established "component-based user story" pattern per someone named Tim's direction: (shared enabler/config) → (reusable component) → (per-page integration), with cross-cutting concerns lifted into their own story. Cited examples: SFCC-104 (BM config, shared) → SFCC-108 (Search filter UI component) → SFCC-199 (PLP integration); SFCC-83 (Recently Viewed shared component) with SFCC-106 (consent) peeled out; SFCC-195 (PDP accordion) as a worked example of slicing by data source, not UI surface.

We also found a local planning doc (dated 2026-06-23, explicitly marked "Draft... to be refined") claiming "Sprint 3" ran 27 Jul–7 Aug 2026 and covered PDP Part 2 + PLP Part 2 + Cart (Squad A) and Search & Recommendations (Squad B) — but the actual git commit history (268 commits total) shows almost none of that landed in the codebase (only one PLP-icons bugfix commit touches PDP/PLP/Cart/Search at all; the actual codebase only has 5 real component folders built so far: button, header, icons, pageContainer, contentful). Today's date is 2026-08-11.

The Jira project key is SFCC (https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/jira, space/site likely "zimmermannworkboard"). Please research and report back on:

1. **Real sprint ground truth**: What are the ACTUAL Jira sprints called, and what are their real date ranges? Use jira_get_agile_boards to find the board, then jira_get_sprints_from_board. Identify which sprint is "Sprint 3" (or whatever is currently active / most recently closed as of 2026-08-11), and pull its actual issue list (jira_get_sprint_issues or jira_get_board_issues) to see what was actually planned and what its current completion status is. Flag clearly if the real sprint numbering/dates/scope differs from the "PDP Part 2/PLP Part 2/Cart/Search" plan described above.

2. **Verify the decomposition pattern is real**: Look up SFCC-104, SFCC-108, SFCC-199, SFCC-83, SFCC-106, SFCC-195, and epic SFCC-1 (jira_get_issue for each). Check current status, the story description/structure, and how granular each is (does one ticket cover one component, or a group of components?). This tells us whether the "component-based" decomposition pattern described above was actually followed, is still in progress, or is mostly aspirational.

3. **Current state of component stories**: Search Jira (jira_search with JQL like `project = SFCC AND text ~ "component"` or similar, and also try text searches for "PDP", "PLP", "Cart", "Search", "filter") for stories that are components-related, in Sprint 3, the current/next sprint, or backlog. For each notable one, report: ticket key, summary, status, story points if present, and — most importantly — whether it's scoped as ONE broad story covering multiple components/a whole page, or as an isolated per-component story. I need concrete examples of both patterns if they exist side by side.

4. **Who is "Tash"?**: Try to identify this person — search Jira users (jira_get_user_profile, or check reporters/assignees on recent component-related and sprint-planning tickets) for a name matching Tash/Natasha/Tasha. She appears to be organizing a "ways of working" alignment meeting, likely a Scrum Master, BA, or Product Owner. Don't guess or fabricate — report only what you can confirm, or say clearly if you can't find a match.

5. **What's queued next**: Check the backlog / upcoming sprint for any stories already queued that reference component work, to see if a NEW isolated/specified-component approach has already started being applied to upcoming tickets, or if everything queued still follows the old broad-story shape.

Report back with concrete ticket keys, summaries, statuses, and direct quotes/paraphrases of story descriptions where relevant — I need specifics to bring into a meeting, not generalities. Organize your report under the 5 numbered questions above. This is research only — do not modify, comment on, or transition any Jira issues. Keep the final report focused and well-structured; it will be read by another Claude session synthesizing a meeting-prep brief, not by an end user directly, so precision and specificity matter more than polish.
